_note: Reviewed one-line situations for every pattern in the pinned fork. Harald's R10: the situation is a DERIVED condition a reader can match their own circumstance against; the README's own paragraph ships verbatim in the entry body. Authored and read in one pass, 2026-08-23.

situations.abstract-document: when objects of one family share some attributes and each type adds its own, and new properties must be addable without changing the classes that read them
situations.abstract-factory: when a system must be configured with one of several families of related objects, and the families must not be mixed
situations.active-object: when an object's methods must run on its own thread so callers are never blocked by its work
situations.actor-model: when concurrent components must communicate only by message and share no mutable state
situations.acyclic-visitor: when a new operation must be added over an existing type hierarchy without modifying it and without every visitor depending on every type
situations.adapter: when an existing class provides the behaviour needed but its interface does not match the one a caller expects
situations.ambassador: when calls to a remote service need retry, timeout, logging or monitoring added without touching the calling code
situations.anti-corruption-layer: when integrating with an external or legacy model whose concepts would distort the local model if let in directly
situations.arrange-act-assert: when a test's setup, action and verification run together and a reader cannot tell which line is being tested
situations.async-method-invocation: when a caller must start long-running work and collect its result later without waiting
situations.backends-for-frontends: when several client types need different shapes of the same data and one shared API is being distorted to serve them all
situations.backpressure: when a producer emits faster than its consumer can process and unbounded buffering would exhaust memory
situations.balking: when an object must ignore a request outright if it is not in a state to honour it
situations.bloc: when UI state changes must flow from events through one place rather than being mutated from many widgets
situations.bridge: when an abstraction and its implementation must vary independently rather than multiplying subclasses for every combination
situations.builder: when an object needs many optional parts and a constructor per combination is unmanageable
situations.business-delegate: when presentation code is coupled to how business services are looked up and invoked
situations.bytecode: when behaviour must be defined as data and executed safely rather than compiled into the program
situations.caching: when the same expensive result is requested repeatedly and recomputing it dominates cost
situations.callback: when a routine must run code supplied by its caller at a point the caller cannot reach
situations.chain-of-responsibility: when a request may be handled by one of several handlers and the sender must not know which
situations.circuit-breaker: when calls to a failing dependency keep being made and each one costs time before failing anyway
situations.clean-architecture: when business rules are entangled with frameworks and the choice of database or UI is hard to change
situations.client-session: when per-client state must survive across requests without being held in the server's own fields
situations.collecting-parameter: when several methods each contribute to one result and returning and merging partial results is awkward
situations.collection-pipeline: when a sequence of collection operations is written as nested loops and the intent is lost in the mechanics
situations.combinator: when small rules must be composed into larger ones at run time rather than written as fixed combinations
situations.command: when a request must be treated as an object so it can be queued, logged, undone or scheduled
situations.command-query-responsibility-segregation: when reads and writes of the same model have such different shapes and loads that one model serves neither well
situations.commander: when a transaction spans several services and any of them may fail after others have committed
situations.component: when behaviour must be composed onto an entity at run time rather than fixed by its class
situations.composite: when clients must treat individual objects and compositions of them uniformly
situations.composite-entity: when a set of interdependent persistent objects must be managed as one unit
situations.composite-view: when a page is assembled from parts that change independently of the page itself
situations.context-object: when protocol-specific state is being passed around and couples unrelated code to the protocol
situations.converter: when two layers hold the same data in different shapes and conversion is scattered across call sites
situations.curiously-recurring-template-pattern: when a base class must refer to the concrete subclass type without casting
situations.currying: when a function takes several arguments and some are known long before the rest
situations.dao-factory: when an application must support several storage backends and the choice must not reach business logic
situations.data-access-object: when persistence details leak into business logic and changing the store means changing that logic
situations.data-bus: when unrelated components must exchange events without knowing about each other
situations.data-locality: when memory access patterns dominate run time and related data is scattered across the heap
situations.data-mapper: when the in-memory model and the database schema must evolve independently of each other
situations.data-transfer-object: when many small remote calls are needed to assemble one result and the round trips dominate
situations.decorator: when responsibilities must be added to individual objects at run time without subclassing every combination
situations.delegation: when behaviour should be reused by forwarding to a helper rather than by inheriting from it
situations.dependency-injection: when a class constructs its own collaborators and therefore cannot be tested or reconfigured
situations.dirty-flag: when an expensive derived value is recomputed on every read though its inputs rarely change
situations.domain-model: when business rules are complex enough that procedural scripts over data become hard to change
situations.double-buffer: when a reader must see a complete state while a writer is still producing the next one
situations.double-checked-locking: when lazily initialised shared state is read far more often than it is written
situations.double-dispatch: when the operation to run depends on the run-time types of two objects, not one
situations.dynamic-proxy: when the same cross-cutting behaviour must wrap many interfaces without writing a wrapper for each
situations.event-aggregator: when a listener must subscribe to many sources and the wiring between them has become unmanageable
situations.event-based-asynchronous: when a caller must be notified of completion rather than waiting for it
situations.event-driven-architecture: when components must react to things that happened without the emitter knowing who reacts
situations.event-queue: when events arrive faster than they can be handled and must be processed in order later
situations.event-sourcing: when the history of how state was reached matters as much as the state itself
situations.execute-around: when a resource must be set up and torn down around caller-supplied work and callers keep forgetting the teardown
situations.extension-objects: when new interfaces must be added to objects without changing their classes or bloating them
situations.facade: when a subsystem's many classes must be used through one simplified entry point
situations.factory: when object creation depends on data and callers should not hold the branching
situations.factory-kit: when a factory's available types must be configured at run time rather than fixed in code
situations.factory-method: when a class cannot know which concrete type to instantiate and subclasses must decide
situations.fallback: when a dependency's failure must degrade the answer rather than fail the request
situations.fanout-fanin: when one request must be split across workers and their results combined before answering
situations.feature-toggle: when behaviour must be switched on or off at run time without redeploying
situations.filterer: when a container's filtering criteria must be composed by callers rather than fixed by the container
situations.fluent-interface: when a sequence of configuration calls reads poorly and the order of steps is easy to get wrong
situations.flux: when UI state is mutated from many places and the flow of a change is impossible to trace
situations.flyweight: when very many objects share most of their state and per-object memory dominates
situations.front-controller: when request handling logic such as auth and routing is duplicated across every entry point
situations.function-composition: when small transformations must be assembled into larger ones without intermediate plumbing
situations.game-loop: when a program must advance simulation and rendering continuously at a controlled rate
situations.gateway: when access to an external system must be isolated behind an interface the local code owns
situations.guarded-suspension: when a thread must wait until a precondition holds rather than fail or spin
situations.half-sync-half-async: when asynchronous arrival and synchronous processing must be separated so neither blocks the other
situations.health-check: when an operator or orchestrator must know whether a service is actually able to serve
situations.hexagonal-architecture: when business logic is coupled to the technologies it happens to be driven by and driving
situations.identity-map: when the same record is loaded more than once in a transaction and duplicate objects diverge
situations.immutable: when an object is shared across threads or used as a map key and its state must never change after construction
situations.intercepting-filter: when pre- and post-processing must be added to requests without touching the handlers
situations.interpreter: when a simple language must be evaluated and its grammar is stable enough to model as classes
situations.iterator: when a collection's contents must be traversed without exposing how it is stored
situations.layered-architecture: when concerns of presentation, logic and data access are mixed in the same classes
situations.lazy-loading: when loading an object eagerly pulls in more data than most callers need
situations.leader-election: when several instances run the same job and exactly one must perform it
situations.leader-followers: when many threads must share one event source without a dispatcher becoming the bottleneck
situations.lockable-object: when concurrent access to a resource must be serialised by ownership rather than by a global lock
situations.map-reduce: when a computation over a large dataset can be split, processed independently and combined
situations.marker-interface: when a type must carry a fact about itself that code can test for without adding behaviour
situations.master-worker: when one unit of work can be divided among workers and their partial results combined
situations.mediator: when a set of objects communicate in a web of direct references that is hard to change
situations.memento: when an object's state must be captured and restored later without exposing its internals
situations.metadata-mapping: when object-to-table mapping is hand-written per class and the same mapping code repeats for every one
situations.microservices-aggregrator: when a client needs one answer assembled from several services and should not call each itself
situations.microservices-api-gateway: when clients must not know the service topology and cross-cutting concerns are duplicated per service
situations.microservices-client-side-ui-composition: when one page is owned by several teams and each must ship its part independently
situations.microservices-distributed-tracing: when a request crosses several services and a failure cannot be followed end to end
situations.microservices-idempotent-consumer: when a message may be delivered more than once and processing it twice would be wrong
situations.microservices-log-aggregation: when logs live per service and diagnosing one request means opening several of them
situations.microservices-messaging: when services must communicate without both being available at the same moment
situations.microservices-self-registration: when instances come and go and their addresses cannot be configured in advance
situations.model-view-controller: when display, input handling and data are mixed in one class and none can change alone
situations.model-view-intent: when UI state must be derived from a stream of user intents rather than mutated in place
situations.model-view-presenter: when view logic must be testable without instantiating the view
situations.model-view-viewmodel: when a view must bind to state declaratively rather than be updated by hand
situations.monad: when a chain of operations each of which may fail or be absent turns into nested conditionals
situations.money: when amounts and currency are carried as bare numbers and rounding or mixing currencies goes unnoticed
situations.monitor: when a shared object's methods must never run concurrently with each other
situations.monolithic-architecture: when a system is small enough that one deployable unit costs less than distributing it
situations.monostate: when all instances of a type must share one state but callers should keep constructing instances
situations.multiton: when exactly one instance per key must exist, rather than one instance overall
situations.mute-idiom: when an exception that genuinely cannot happen forces boilerplate at every call site
situations.naked-objects: when the user interface should be derived from the domain objects rather than written separately
situations.notification: when several validation failures must be collected and reported together rather than thrown one at a time
situations.null-object: when callers are peppered with null checks for an absent collaborator
situations.object-mother: when tests each build the same fixture objects by hand and drift apart as the model changes
situations.object-pool: when creating an object is expensive and instances can safely be reused
situations.observer: when several objects must react to a subject's change without the subject knowing them
situations.onion-architecture: when dependencies point outward from the domain and infrastructure choices are hard to replace
situations.optimistic-offline-lock: when concurrent edits are rare and holding a lock across a user's think time is unacceptable
situations.page-controller: when each page's request handling is duplicated and cannot vary per page
situations.page-object: when UI tests break on every markup change because selectors are spread through them
situations.parameter-object: when the same group of arguments travels together through many signatures
situations.partial-response: when clients need different subsets of a resource and fetching all of it is wasteful
situations.pipeline: when a transformation is a fixed sequence of stages that must be reordered or reused independently
situations.poison-pill: when consumer threads must be told to stop through the same channel they receive work on
situations.polling-publisher: when a source cannot push and changes must still be detected and published
situations.presentation-model: when view state and view behaviour must be testable without the widget toolkit
situations.private-class-data: when a class exposes mutable state that should be fixed after construction
situations.producer-consumer: when work is generated and processed at different rates and must be decoupled by a buffer
situations.promise: when a result that is not available yet must be passed around and composed
situations.property: when an object's attributes must be added and removed at run time rather than declared
situations.prototype: when constructing an object is costly and an existing instance can be copied instead
situations.proxy: when access to an object must be controlled, deferred or instrumented without the client knowing
situations.publish-subscribe: when messages must reach any number of interested parties the sender does not know
situations.queue-based-load-leveling: when bursts of requests would overwhelm a service that can only work at a steady rate
situations.rate-limiting-pattern: when a client or caller must be held to a maximum request rate to protect a resource
situations.reactor: when many connections must be served by few threads, driven by readiness events
situations.registry: when well-known objects must be found without passing them through every layer
situations.repository: when domain code queries the database directly and query logic is spread through it
situations.resource-acquisition-is-initialization: when a resource must be released exactly once, on every path out of a scope
situations.retry: when a failure is likely transient and one more attempt would probably succeed
situations.role-object: when an object must present different interfaces to different clients and gain roles at run time
situations.rule-engine: when business rules change more often than the code around them and are buried in branching
situations.saga: when a business transaction spans services that cannot share one commit
situations.separated-interface: when a caller must depend on an interface whose implementation lives in a package it must not know
situations.serialized-entity: when an object must be stored and restored whole rather than mapped field by field
situations.serialized-lob: when a small object graph is always read together and mapping it to tables costs more than it returns
situations.servant: when the same behaviour is needed by several classes that should not inherit it
situations.server-session: when session state is kept per client on the server and must be found by an identifier
situations.service-layer: when application logic is duplicated across UIs and transaction boundaries are unclear
situations.service-locator: when collaborators must be found at run time and constructing them per call is wasteful
situations.service-stub: when a test depends on a slow or unavailable external service
situations.service-to-worker: when request handling must dispatch to logic and then choose a view, in that order
situations.session-facade: when clients make many fine-grained calls to a set of business objects across a network
situations.sharding: when one store cannot hold or serve the whole dataset and it must be partitioned by key
situations.single-table-inheritance: when a class hierarchy is small and mapping each subclass to its own table costs more joins than it saves
situations.singleton: when exactly one instance must exist and be reachable from anywhere
situations.spatial-partition: when finding nearby objects means testing every object against every other
situations.special-case: when the same conditional handling of an absent or exceptional value repeats across callers
situations.specification: when selection rules must be combined and reused rather than written per query
situations.state: when an object's behaviour changes with its state and the branching on that state has spread
situations.step-builder: when construction has a required order and callers can currently skip or reorder steps
situations.strangler: when a legacy system must be replaced incrementally while it keeps serving traffic
situations.strategy: when an algorithm must be chosen at run time and its variants are branching inside one method
situations.subclass-sandbox: when subclasses need a set of operations provided by their base rather than reaching outside
situations.table-inheritance: when a class hierarchy must be persisted with each class's own table
situations.table-module: when logic applies uniformly to all rows of a table and per-object logic is unnecessary
situations.template-method: when several implementations share a fixed sequence of steps but differ in individual steps
situations.templateview: when a view is mostly static markup with holes to fill rather than logic
situations.thread-pool-executor: when tasks arrive faster than threads should be created for them
situations.thread-specific-storage: when state must be per thread and passing it through every call is impractical
situations.throttling: when a consumer's resource use must be capped so one tenant cannot starve the others
situations.tolerant-reader: when a message's shape may gain fields and a strict reader would break on them
situations.trampoline: when a recursive algorithm is deep enough to exhaust the call stack
situations.transaction-script: when each business action is a simple procedure and a full domain model is more than the problem needs
situations.twin: when a class must effectively extend two hierarchies and the language allows only one
situations.type-object: when new kinds of a thing must be added as data rather than as new classes
situations.unit-of-work: when several changes must be tracked and committed together rather than written one at a time
situations.update-method: when many objects must each advance one step per frame or tick
situations.value-object: when two objects with the same attributes should be considered equal and neither should change
situations.version-number: when concurrent updates must be detected without locking the record
situations.view-helper: when a view contains logic that should not be written in the template
situations.virtual-proxy: when an expensive object should not be created until it is actually used
situations.visitor: when new operations must be added over a stable type hierarchy without changing its classes
